subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should ACP `sessions_spawn` gain an OpenClaw skill-context carrier, and if so should it start as explicit skill ids only or include default/auto selection?
rationale: The feature crosses ACP child prompt, session-state, and security boundaries by copying local skill context into external harnesses, so automation should not choose the permanent selection, redaction, prompt-layer, and audit contract.

options.title: Explicit audited carrier first
options.body: Add only explicit `skills: [...]` selection at first, with size/hash/redaction/selection metadata and focused ACP/Codex parity tests before considering default or automatic selection.

options.title: Broader default/auto design
options.body: Keep the issue open for a larger product design that includes default skill sets, automatic relevance, observability, and resume semantics together.

options.title: Defer to harness-native skills
options.body: Do not inject OpenClaw-rendered skill material through ACP spawn and instead document existing per-agent filters plus native Codex or ACPX skill setup paths.

recommendation.title: Explicit audited carrier first
recommendation.body: Add only explicit `skills: [...]` selection at first, with size/hash/redaction/selection metadata and focused ACP/Codex parity tests before considering default or automatic selection.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the related maintainer-labeled prompt-contract discussion that overlaps the product choice here.
